Why this person for this seat

Built for the deals Profound is winning now

Profound’s enterprise deals now run through procurement, legal and security review, and they’re priced on usage. Both are where I’ve spent my career.

The budget sits outside marketing

I sold marketing platforms mainly to CIOs, CTOs and CFOs, because they owned the budget. I was the Digital Account Executive on Loblaw and Walmart, where Marketing Cloud was the largest and lead contract.

Consumption is already my language

Profound’s Enterprise plan is priced on AI Marketer credits, with unlimited seats. I trained my team to be the first sellers at Salesforce responsible for Data Cloud on multiple consumption strategies, which evolved into Flex Credits. Before that, I sold CDP consumption myself.

I build teams from zero

I built a 10-person US Enterprise AI and Digital sales team from scratch across six offices, delivering better than 30% of vertical revenue. Before Salesforce, I spent 3.5 years as a first-line manager with full P&L ownership.

Two ways I can help

A US team now. Canada next.

The segment can flex. What stays fixed is that I lead the team, whether it wins new business or grows Profound’s largest customers.

Now

Lead a US team, from Toronto

Mid-Market or Enterprise sales, or Strategic Customer Success. My last team managed the strategic contracts and the use of data, AI and marketing technology at Williams Sonoma, Kroger, PepsiCo, Coca-Cola, Mars, Walmart and many of the largest US retail and consumer goods companies. Walmart already uses Profound. Toronto runs on New York’s time zone, and I’ve led a US team from here.

For a sales team: multi-threading into IT, security and finance early, MEDDPICC inspection on every deal, and a business case the buyer can defend internally. For Strategic Customer Success: executive business reviews and an expansion plan for every top account, built on how its credits are used. I oversaw delivery from signature through adoption on virtually every deal I sold.

Next

Canada, when you’re ready

The hard part of a new country is the first year: first hires, first reference customers, and answers on French-language coverage and Quebec’s privacy law. Someone who already knows Profound’s product, playbook and people shortens that year.

  • Canadian enterprise buying is concentrated in a small number of retail, grocery, banking and telecom groups in Toronto and Montréal.
  • I’ve sold to Loblaw, Walmart Canada, Home Depot Canada, Roots, Indigo, LCBO and SAQ.

I’d rather join before Canada than be hired for it.

Operating plan

The first 180 days

A starting plan built from public information. I’d test every assumption against what the revenue team already knows.

Days 0–30Learn the motion
  • Sit in on enterprise deals and learn how Prompt Volumes, Answer Engine Insights and the AI Marketer land with buyers.
  • Learn how credit packages are sized, and where deals slow in security, legal and procurement.
  • Meet the Engagement and Solutions teams who carry delivery after signature.
Days 30–90Lead and coach
  • Take on the team you need most: Mid-Market, Enterprise or Strategic Customer Success.
  • Inspect every deal against MEDDPICC with an economic buyer and champion named early, or every top account against an expansion plan.
  • Build a credit-sizing business case: what a 1% gain on the customer’s top objective is worth, so the package pays for itself on paper.
Days 90–180Write the Canada case
  • Size the opportunity in Canada’s largest brands and name the first reference customers to win.
  • Put a written entry plan in front of revenue leadership: timing, first hires, French-language coverage and privacy review.
  • Keep the US number the priority until leadership says go.
